clue.text: Distances travelled over two days in former time

indicators.note: the distances word is spread over the pair of days, covering them on both sides

parts.note: mileages are distances travelled
D is the abbreviation for day, so two days give DD

explanation.surface: A traveller totting up the miles covered across a couple of days in some bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering on both sides, an unusual containment signal; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval period is a historical era long past, so it is a former time.

clue.text: Virtues displayed by monarch in swirling mist

indicators.note: the monarch is placed in the middle of the rearranged mist letters
mist that swirls is stirred about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: A queen emerging from swirling fog, showing her good qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' is just a link; 'swirling' gives MITS, which 'in' opens up after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Merits are good qualities or strengths, the same as virtues.

clue.text: Edges of double bed cut down to size

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, here of double

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed

explanation.surface: Trimming the sides of a double bed to make it fit the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk a claim is to deflate or expose it, figuratively cutting it down to size.

clue.text: County site here with relics abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An archaeological dig left deserted, its finds left lying about in some English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder, SITE HERE and RELICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicestershire is a county in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Greeting Scottish banker and a rising religious leader

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
a banker is a river (it has banks); the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: Someone saying hello to a Scottish bank employee and an ascending cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses HALLO + TAY + A, which read upwards give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shia Muslim cleric, a religious leader in Iran.

clue.text: Compound fracture reset

indicators.note: to fracture is to break, so the letters of reset are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor resetting a compound fracture, a broken bone through the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound fracture' reads as one medical term, but it splits into definition and anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is a chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Impressive eastern prince seen regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from prince gives its odd letters

explanation.surface: An oriental prince who is often seen and makes a fine impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand or heroic in scale, hence impressive.

clue.text: Endlessly support excessively distant diplomatic code?

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its final letter, having no end

parts.note: a prop is a support
too means excessively
cold means distant or aloof

explanation.surface: Backing an aloof diplomatic stance without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last letter from each of PROP, TOO and COLD, giving PRO, TO and COL.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal etiquette and rules governing diplomatic conduct; the question mark admits it is a loose description.

clue.text: Shield of wood old so kept in historic island

indicators.note: the short pieces are kept inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete, home of the ancient Minoan civilisation, is a historic island

explanation.surface: An ancient wooden shield preserved in a museum on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a tar-based preservative painted on timber to protect it from rot, a shield for wood.

clue.text: How one might face Grandmaster or General?

definitions.text: How one might face Grandmaster or General?

parts.words: How one might face Grandmaster or General?
parts.note: a chess master is literally faced over the chessboard, and in military games a general across a war table; also a phrase meaning applying to all

explanation.walkthrough: Opponents at chess sit facing each other over a board; the phrase also means universally, which 'General' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means applying to everyone equally, while literally describing opponents seated at a chessboard.

clue.text: Animal ultimately out for synagogue official

indicators.note: the ultimate (final) letter of the animal is put out

parts.note: a rabbit is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal banned from the synagogue by an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher who leads a synagogue congregation.

clue.text: Vegetable all right in acre hit disastrously

indicators.note: the letters for all right go in among the rearranged letters
something done disastrously goes wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: OK means all right

explanation.surface: A vegetable crop survives a field hit badly by weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'acre hit' as a field struck by disaster; 'disastrously' actually makes ARTICHE, which 'in' opens near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle whose flower buds are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Fruit to put round sort of cake

indicators.note: the word to is put round the cake piece, enclosing it

parts.note: angel cake is a light sponge

explanation.surface: Arranging fruit around a cake as decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Brazilian city as far as we're concerned ungovernable

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city
to us means in our view

explanation.surface: A view that a Brazilian city is out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous means wild and disorderly, beyond being controlled.

clue.text: Complaint that feels too contrived?

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that something seems far too artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests a grievance but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlete's foot is a fungal skin infection, a medical complaint in the sense of a minor illness.

clue.text: Musician perhaps a boastful person?

definitions.meaning: a player of a brass instrument
one who blows their own trumpet, i.e. boasts

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a musician might be a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays a brass horn is one, and the idiom of blowing one's own horn makes it a braggart.

clue.text: Founder lacking sparkle after trip

indicators.note: the sparkle-less word comes after the trip word

parts.note: to trip is to fall
flat drink has lost its fizz

explanation.surface: A company's founder, dull and uninspired, after stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a person who sets something up, but it is the verb meaning to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: To founder is to collapse or fail, as does a joke or plan that falls flat.

clue.text: Way forest officer shows new face

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a ranger patrols a forest or park

explanation.surface: A forest warden showing a newcomer the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link word between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfamiliar, never met before, is a new face.

clue.text: Fatter, out of shape, nevertheless tucking in? Here's further idea

indicators.note: the word for nevertheless is tucked inside the rearranged letters
out of shape signals the letters are bent into a new form

parts.note: though means nevertheless

explanation.surface: Someone getting fatter yet still eating heartily has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking in' pretends to be about eating; 'out of shape' makes AFTERT, and the insertion lands just before its final letter. 'Here's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterthought is an idea added later, a further idea.

clue.text: Alfresco meal and walk in park

explanation.surface: Eating outdoors and strolling in a park.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor food on a blanket is one sense; the idiom 'no picnic' shows the other sense of an easy task.

clue.text: Clever little rodent died

parts.note: a shrew is a small mouse-like creature

explanation.surface: A clever small creature that has died.
explanation.walkthrough: A shrew is not strictly a rodent, but clues often treat it as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute and sharp in judgement.

clue.text: Hide ecstasy in panic

indicators.note: the drug letter goes inside the panic word

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Concealing drugs while in a state of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned animal skin is both a hide and a leather.

clue.text: Continental river horse perhaps? Sounds like it

indicators.note: the clue says the river's name sounds like the horse word

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat

explanation.surface: A European river's name seems to evoke a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major river of France and Switzerland on the European continent.

clue.text: One getting into remixed Bush LP issue

indicators.note: the digit-like letter gets into the rearranged letters
a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I resembles the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fan getting into a remixed Kate Bush album being released.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate Bush is a British singer, so 'Bush LP' reads as an album; 'remixed' makes PUBLSH, opened by 'getting into' near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or record is to bring it out to the public.

clue.text: Prisoner released by nobleman not a violent drunk?

parts.note: a lag is a convict, especially an old lag

indicators.note: not a means the a is removed from the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
out means freed from prison

explanation.surface: A convict freed thanks to an aristocrat, who insists he is not a violent drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: A lager lout is a British term for a young man made rowdy and aggressive by drinking beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A loutish beer drinker who turns aggressive is a violent drunk; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: One German artist back for Schwarzenegger?

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: ein is German for one
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A German-speaking painter returning to stand in for an Austrian actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnie is the familiar nickname of the actor Arnold Schwarzenegger; the question mark flags the pet name.

clue.text: Aviator at last seen in barrel roll

indicators.note: the picked letter is seen in the barrel word

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of aviator

explanation.surface: A pilot finally performing a barrel roll stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrel roll' reads as one aerobatic term but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of the dice or a rotation is a turn.

clue.text: Expert contracted to provide cover had issue

indicators.note: the contracted word wraps round and covers the expert

parts.note: reduced means made smaller
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist hired to provide insurance cover had a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had issue' looks like trouble but means had offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so to have issue is to bear children, i.e. reproduce.
